question: Can the deployed generated-candidate primitive interface and the complete released skill execute a first pick-lift-transport-release chain on unchanged original layouts?

conditions.name: single_cycle
conditions.description: Frozen stage40 candidate, only outer loop six to one. Same perception, action primitives, corrected rejection wrapper and gripper retention.

conditions.name: released_first_basket_cycle
conditions.description: Released controller with first-source processing through its first basket transfer attempt; preserve internal qualification/recovery/handoff, stop further task iteration. Richer interface, descriptive capability reference only.

primary_unit: one source-to-basket attempt per original development layout; deployment failures separate
metrics: lift root rise and held object motion proxies
native task score and full success separately
first failure phase and unused interface requirements
limits: Not an equal-interface causal comparison between conditions.
Different native selectors may choose different objects; no paired score superiority inference.
One cycle cannot establish full multi-object task success.
Simulator state is analysis-only and is never supplied to a controller.
Same five exposed layouts; no independent generalization.
Object root rise and co-motion are kinematic proxies, not force/contact proofs.
followup: Complete this capability route and analyze before new System2 generation; no automatic enlargement of scenario/model search.
